Summary of the Amazon S3 Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region

February 28, 2017

On the morning of February 28, 2017, the Amazon S3 team was debugging an issue causing the S3 billing system to progress more slowly than expected. At 9:37AM PST, an authorized S3 team member using an established playbook executed a command which was intended to remove a small number of servers for one of the S3 subsystems. Unfortunately, one of the inputs to the command was entered incorrectly and a larger set of servers was removed than intended.

The servers that were inadvertently removed supported two other S3 subsystems: the index subsystem and the placement subsystem. The removal of a significant portion of the capacity caused each of these systems to require a full restart.

While these subsystems were being restarted, S3 was unable to service requests. Amazon S3 restoration took approximately 4 hours. We have modified the tool so that it can only remove servers within a safety threshold.

Root cause: an operational playbook permitted a single-parameter error to cross two independent capacity thresholds simultaneously. The S3 service had grown significantly since its launch and had not performed a full restart of these subsystems for many years, so the restart time was longer than expected.
